channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: 6 states have primaries Tuesday. Here's what you need to know
item.description: A democratic socialist has shaken up the race for Wisconsin governor and Minnesota also sees a battle between a progressive and a moderate in primaries also fought in South Carolina.

item.title: Primaries in Wisconsin and Minnesota pit progressives against moderates
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks Jessica Taylor of the Cook Political Report about battles between moderate and progressive candidates in Tuesday's Democratic primaries in Wisconsin and Minnesota.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Leila Fadel asks Jessica Taylor of the Cook Political Report about battles between moderate and progressive candidates in Tuesday's Democratic primaries in Wisconsin and Minnesota.

item.title: Trump issues executive order aimed at upending vaccines for kids
item.description: President Trump issued another executive order Monday, attempting to scramble how children are vaccinated in the United States.

item.title: A midwife crosses 'maternity deserts' to make a difference for Black moms and babies
item.description: New research from the March of Dimes says more than half of U.S. counties have no labor and delivery hospitals. One Black midwife tries to make a difference for moms in Alabama.

item.title: New book explores the cultural impact of Paul Simon's signature album, 'Graceland'
item.description: A new book celebrates the 40th anniversary of Paul Simon's signature album, "Graceland." NPR's A Martinez speaks with Ashley Kahn, author of "Days of Miracle and Wonder."

item.title: After redrawing congressional map, Alabama voters head to the polls -- again
item.description: Some voters in Alabama will be casting ballots for a second time in their congressional primary Tuesday. It's the result of a redistricting effort that followed a Supreme Court ruling.

item.title: Team works to identify WWII soldier who died in Alaskan plane crash
item.description: In Sitka, Alaska, a Defense Department team has exhumed the remains of an unidentified WWII soldier, in hopes of identification and reburial in a place of his family's choosing.

item.title: How are schools adjusting sports for student athletes as sweltering heat lingers
item.description: As a new school year approaches, student athletes across Texas are returning to the field for fall sports, even as punishing heat lingers. How are rules and practices changing?
